title: Operation Sky — Skype group sharing abuse material
who: Invitation-only Skype group with members from 14 countries
what: Spanish police followed Tor links to a private Skype group whose members from 14 countries exchanged abuse material; by May 2018 eight people had been arrested in France, Hungary, Italy, Spain and Canada.

title: Bergisch Gladbach abuse complex
who: Chat groups of men sharing recordings of abuse of their own and other children
network: North Rhine-Westphalia abuse complexes (Lügde, Bergisch Gladbach)
what: In October 2019 police found a large cache of child abuse images and videos at a house in Bergisch Gladbach; the man there had repeatedly abused his daughter, born in 2017, and shared recordings in chat groups. On 6 October 2020 Cologne Regional Court sentenced him to 12 years plus preventive detention. Investigators found more than 30,000 pseudonyms used in the network, many untraceable; by January 2022 Cologne police had identified 439 suspects, secured numerous convictions and rescued 65 children aged from three months to 17. Two other men, from Krefeld and Viersen, were sentenced to 14.5 and 13.5 years.

title: Operación Roblox — extortion network in Panama
who: A man in Puerto Caimito, La Chorrera (Panamá Oeste), arrested in 'Operación Roblox'
what: On 23 October 2024 Panama's National Police and Public Ministry carried out 'Operación Roblox' in Puerto Caimito, La Chorrera district, arresting a man accused of illicit contact with minors through the Roblox gaming platform and of threatening them to demand child sexual abuse material. The alert came from Spanish police investigating a child sexual abuse material network; phones and laptops were seized and investigations were continuing.

title: Gulf states block Roblox over child safety (2025)
who: Roblox Corporation
what: In August 2025 Qatar blocked access to Roblox (13 August) and Kuwait's telecoms regulator temporarily blocked it (21 August) after parents and community groups raised child-safety concerns; Turkey had blocked it on 7 August. Roblox had been banned in Oman and Jordan since 2020, and was banned in the UAE from 2018 to 2021. Wikipedia additionally reports that Bahraini MPs drafted a ban, Palestine announced a ban in November 2025, Kazakhstan's and Kyrgyzstan's authorities warned parents about predators, and Buenos Aires and three Argentine provinces blocked it on school devices after grooming reports.

title: Brazil orders Discord to suspend livestreaming (2026)
who: Discord Inc.
what: On 12 August 2026 Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) ordered Discord to suspend its livestreaming feature nationwide, saying it had found 'robust evidence' that Discord failed to take reasonable steps to stop minors being exposed to content promoting violence, self-harm and suicide. The order followed the death in July 2026 of a 13-year-old girl in central-western Brazil who, authorities said, was encouraged during a Discord livestream to take her own life. Five teenagers were arrested in connection with her death, and police said the investigation also led them to another girl at risk, whom they reached in time. A Justice Ministry cyber-intelligence official called the case 'a terrible failure in moderation'.

title: Operation Hamlet — parents sharing abuse of their own children
who: International online network of offenders, many abusing their own children
what: Danish National Police, acting on information from Save the Children about images found online, arrested a man and his wife who had posted images of the abuse of their nine-year-old daughter; from November 2001 the US Customs CyberSmuggling Center coordinated US inquiries with Danish police, INTERPOL and NCMEC. On 9 August 2002 US Customs announced 10 arrests of US citizens, with 10 more suspects arrested in Denmark, Belgium, Germany, England, Switzerland and the Netherlands, and 45 children rescued, 37 of them in the US; in many cases parents were abusing their own children. Fifteen suspects, five of them foreign nationals, were indicted on federal conspiracy charges in the Eastern District of California on 8 August 2002.

title: Operation Long Arm — 'Bamse' bulletin board (1992)
who: Bamse BBS (Danish bulletin board, ~900 users)
what: US Customs' first major case against internet child abuse material. In late 1992 a US Customs controlled delivery led to a suspect who said he had obtained images from a Europe-based bulletin board; agents found 'Bamse', a Danish bulletin board with child abuse rooms, and two other Danish boards using its images, where users paid a subscription or supplied images of their own. Working with Danish authorities, the operation led to about 35 arrests and convictions in the US. Start year approximate.

title: Operation Soteria Shield (North Texas, 2025–2026)
who: FBI Dallas, North Texas ICAC Task Force, over 70 agencies, NCMEC
what: FBI Dallas and the North Texas Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, with about 70 law enforcement agencies, ran the operation against online child exploitation. The first round, which began in April 2025 and lasted about a month, led to 244 people being charged and 109 children rescued, announced in June 2025. A second, two-month round, announced on 29 May 2026, led to 276 arrests and 89 children rescued across Texas, mostly on charges of possessing or distributing child sexual abuse material; authorities said cases remained active.

title: Matthew Falder — dark web 'hurtcore' blackmailer
who: Individual offender posting on hurtcore dark web sites
cover_up: The NCA said technology companies' limited cooperation may have delayed identifying victims.
what: A Cambridge-educated Birmingham university researcher posed online as a depressed female artist to lure victims, some as young as 14, into sending images, then blackmailed them into sending increasingly degrading material, which he shared on dark web 'hurtcore' sites. The NCA estimated more than 50 victims between 2009 and 2017. A taskforce of the NCA, GCHQ, US Homeland Security Investigations, the Australian Federal Police and Europol, with police in Israel and Slovenia, identified him after four years; he was arrested in June 2017. He admitted 137 of 188 charges and was jailed for 32 years in February 2018, thought to be the first UK prosecution related to hurtcore material; in October 2018 the Court of Appeal reduced the sentence to 25 years.

title: NCMEC 2025: generative AI in 1.5 million reports
who: NCMEC CyberTipline
what: NCMEC's first look at 2025 data: over 1.5 million reports had a generative-AI connection, 1.1 million of them from Amazon AI Services with no actionable information. Excluding those: 12,000+ involved CSAM in AI training data, 7,000+ users generating or possessing AI CSAM, 30,000+ attempts to generate CSAM from uploaded images, 145,000+ altering CSAM files. NCMEC says more than 275 victims of AI-generated CSAM have been identified since 2023.

title: Spanish town: boys made AI nude images of 20 girls
who: Teenage boys using a 'nudify' website
what: In September 2023, at the start of the school year in Almendralejo (Extremadura), AI-generated nude images of schoolgirls made with an app circulated in at least four of the town's five middle schools; more than 20 girls were affected, including girls aged 12 and 14. Police received at least seven complaints and identified several of the alleged authors, and the case was referred to the Juvenile Prosecutor's Office.

title: Kik Messenger — groups distributing abuse material
who: Kik Messenger
what: In March 2016 the arrest of a registered sex offender uncovered more than 200 Kik groups dedicated to distributing and selling child abuse material. A UK police investigator said delays in getting information from the company increased risk to children. Kik joined the Virtual Global Taskforce in 2015 and added image-detection in October 2016.

title: Operation Protect Our Children — domain seizures (2011)
who: US ICE HSI
cover_up: Seizure of one shared domain redirected about 84,000 unrelated subdomains to a seizure warning.
what: In February 2011 ICE Homeland Security Investigations and the US Justice Department, under a court order obtained without notice to owners, seized about ten domain names alleged to be advertising or distributing child sexual abuse material. One seized domain belonged to a free shared DNS provider, so late on 11 February 2011 all 84,000 of its subdomains, mostly unrelated small websites, displayed the ICE seizure notice; the seizure was reversed within about two days.

title: Rotherham — Jay inquiry (1,400 children, 1997–2013)
who: Group-based exploitation networks; Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council; South Yorkshire Police
cover_up: Three earlier reports (2002, 2003, 2013) on exploitation were effectively suppressed or ignored; police did not treat the abuse as a priority.
what: Professor Alexis Jay's independent inquiry, published 26 August 2014, estimated that about 1,400 children were sexually exploited in Rotherham between 1997 and 2013, some as young as 11. It described the collective failures of the council and South Yorkshire Police as 'blatant'. The report said most known perpetrators were of Pakistani heritage, and that frontline staff were confused about what might be seen as racist. The council leader resigned within hours of publication.

title: Operation Stovewood — NCA Rotherham investigation
who: National Crime Agency investigation into non-recent exploitation in Rotherham
what: The National Crime Agency took over the Rotherham investigation in 2014. Its page reports about 1,150 potential victims identified, more than 220 people arrested or interviewed voluntarily, and 39 people convicted with about 470 years of prison sentences. On 8 August 2025 the NCA agreed to take over an investigation, directed by the Independent Office for Police Conduct, into allegations of child sexual abuse by former South Yorkshire Police officers (allegations; no finding yet).

title: Rochdale — Operation Span convictions and 2024 review
who: Grooming network linked to two takeaway restaurants; Greater Manchester Police; Rochdale Council
cover_up: Police identified ring-leaders in 2007 but did not pursue them; Operation Span launched over two years after the first reports.
what: In May 2012 nine men were convicted after Operation Span, which Greater Manchester Police began in December 2010, more than two years after it was first told of abuse linked to two takeaways. Girls as young as 12 were plied with drink and drugs and passed between men for cash. A 173-page review published 15 January 2024 found children were 'left at the mercy' of gangs between 2004 and 2013 through a 'lamentable strategic failure' of senior police and council leaders; it identified hundreds of potential victims, mainly white girls from poor backgrounds, abused by Asian men, and said 96 men were still a potential risk to children.

title: Oxford — Operation Bullfinch and 2015 Serious Case Review
who: Grooming network; Thames Valley Police; Oxfordshire County Council
what: Seven men were jailed in May 2013 for a combined minimum of 95 years after Operation Bullfinch; the trial judge said police and social services missed tell-tale signs. The Oxfordshire Serious Case Review, published 3 March 2015, estimated that more than 350 young people were sexually exploited in the county from 1999 to 2014. It found police did not believe the girls and treated them as if they had chosen their situation, and social services knew of grooming but failed to protect them. Both the police and council apologised.

title: Telford — Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Exploitation
who: Group-based exploitation networks; West Mercia Police; Telford & Wrekin Council
cover_up: Concerns raised by officers, youth workers and teachers in the 1990s were not taken seriously; specialist CSE teams were cut to near zero after Operation Chalice.
what: The inquiry chaired by Tom Crowther QC, published 12 July 2022, found more than 1,000 children were sexually exploited in Telford over at least 30 years. Agencies dismissed the abuse as 'child prostitution', blamed children for 'lifestyle choices', and failed to investigate partly from nervousness about race. Seven men were jailed in 2013 after Operation Chalice. West Mercia Police and the council apologised; the inquiry found no evidence of corruption.

title: Newcastle — Operation Sanctuary
who: Grooming networks; Northumbria Police
what: Operation Sanctuary began in 2014 and led to 18 people being jailed for sexually abusing girls and young women they had groomed in Newcastle. The Joint Serious Case Review, published 23 February 2018, put the number of victims at about 700 across the Northumbria area, 108 of them in Newcastle. It found no evidence that concerns about political correctness or accusations of racism made police reluctant to investigate, and called for law changes on sexual exploitation.

title: Huddersfield — Operation Tendersea
who: Grooming networks; West Yorkshire Police investigation
what: In October 2018, 20 men were convicted at Leeds Crown Court of abusing girls as young as 11 in Huddersfield between 2004 and 2011; the ringleader's convictions involved 11 girls. By April 2023 Operation Tendersea had convicted 42 men in several trials for abuse between 1995 and 2013, with 505 years and six months of sentences.

title: Derby — Operation Retriever
who: Grooming network; Derbyshire Police investigation
what: Derbyshire Police's Operation Retriever led to the conviction of nine men in 2010 for grooming and sexually abusing 26 girls, one aged 12. Thirteen men had been charged and eleven stood trial.

title: Halifax/Calderdale — West Yorkshire grooming trials
who: Grooming networks; West Yorkshire Police
what: On 6 November 2024, 20 men were jailed for more than 200 years combined for raping and abusing four girls aged 12 to 16 in Calderdale between 2001 and 2010, after three West Yorkshire Police investigations. In May 2026 six more men were convicted over the abuse of one girl from 2006 to 2009, which she reported to police in 2019.

title: Keighley — 2016 convictions
who: Grooming network
what: In February 2016 twelve men were jailed, with sentences of up to 20 years, for sexually exploiting a vulnerable teenage girl in Keighley. A further six men were jailed in 2022 for the systematic rape of another teenage girl in the town.

title: Oldham — 2022 assurance review
who: Oldham Council; Greater Manchester Police; shisha bars, residential homes and taxis
what: The review published 20 June 2022 found 'serious failings' by Oldham Council and Greater Manchester Police: police and council knew of risks from shisha bars by late 2010 yet children of 13 and 14 still visited them in 2013, and multi-agency child-protection procedures were often not started. It criticised how a former council welfare rights officer, later convicted of rape and trafficking, was investigated. The review found no evidence of a cover-up by senior managers or councillors. Oldham is the first confirmed area for local investigation under the 2025 national inquiry.

title: Casey national audit on group-based child sexual exploitation
who: Home Office; police forces in England and Wales
what: Baroness Casey's audit, published 16 June 2025, found that data flaws meant the scale of group-based exploitation could not be assessed, and that perpetrator ethnicity was not recorded for about two-thirds of cases. Local data from three police force areas showed 'disproportionate numbers of men from Asian ethnic backgrounds amongst suspects', which she said warranted further examination; she said flawed data had been used to dismiss concerns. The government accepted all 12 recommendations, including mandatory ethnicity and nationality data for suspects, charging adult sex with under-16s as rape, an NCA-led national operation, and a national inquiry with statutory powers.

title: Home Office paper on group-based CSE characteristics (2020)
who: Home Office
what: The Home Office paper published 15 December 2020 reviewed the evidence on group-based child sexual exploitation. It said research found group-based offenders were 'most commonly White' and that available data did not support conclusions that any one ethnic group was over-represented, while stressing that data were poor and inconsistently recorded. The Home Secretary's foreword said community and cultural factors were 'clearly relevant'. The 2025 Casey audit later said such flawed data had been used to dismiss concerns.

title: Independent Inquiry into Grooming Gangs (2025–)
who: National panel overseeing local investigations
what: On 9 December 2025 the Home Secretary named Baroness Anne Longfield, former Children's Commissioner, as chair of a national inquiry with full statutory powers overseeing local investigations into grooming gangs, following Casey's recommendation. It is time-limited to three years with a £65m budget, will hold individuals and institutions to account, and Oldham is the first confirmed local investigation. Final terms of reference were due by March 2026.

title: Backpage.com — seizure, CEO plea and owners' convictions
who: Backpage.com classified advertising website
what: US authorities seized Backpage.com in April 2018. On 12 April 2018 CEO Carl Ferrer pleaded guilty to conspiracy to facilitate prostitution and money laundering; the Justice Department said the site earned hundreds of millions of dollars from 'escort' ads and that traffickers used it to advertise children and adults alike. In November 2023 a Phoenix jury convicted co-owners Scott Spear and John Brunst on Travel Act and money-laundering counts and Michael Lacey on one count of international concealment money laundering; co-founder James Larkin died on 31 July 2023 before trial. On 28 August 2024 Spear and Brunst were sentenced to 10 years and Lacey to five; DOJ said the scheme earned more than $500 million.

title: Craigslist adult services closure (2010)
who: Craigslist
what: In September 2010 Craigslist removed its 'adult services' section from its US site, replacing it with a 'censored' label, after a letter from 18 state attorneys general led by Connecticut's Richard Blumenthal. The letter said the section carried rampant prostitution ads and facilitated human trafficking, including ads involving children. Blumenthal estimated the section could generate over $36 million in revenue. Much of the advertising later moved to Backpage, which AGs urged to close its own section that month.

title: Pornhub/MindGeek (Aylo) — card cut-off, DOJ agreement and FTC/Utah settlement
who: Aylo Holdings (formerly MindGeek), owner of Pornhub
what: After a New York Times column by Nicholas Kristof on 4 December 2020 reported child sexual abuse material and non-consensual videos on Pornhub, the site banned uploads from unverified users and Mastercard (10 Dec 2020) and Visa stopped card acceptance. On 21 December 2023 Aylo entered a deferred prosecution agreement in Brooklyn over unlawful monetary transactions involving sex-trafficking proceeds (linked to GirlsDoPorn, whose victims were adult women), paying over $1.8 million plus victim compensation and accepting a three-year monitor; Aylo did not plead guilty. On 3 September 2025 Aylo agreed to pay $5 million to the FTC and Utah, which alleged it knowingly profited from child sexual abuse material and that its fingerprinting system was ineffective from at least 2017 to August 2021.

title: FBI Operation Cross Country XIII (2023)
who: FBI and partner agencies
what: During a two-week operation in July 2023, announced 1 August 2023, the FBI and partners identified and located 200 sex-trafficking victims, including 59 minor victims of child sex trafficking and sexual exploitation, and located 59 actively missing children. 68 trafficking suspects and 126 suspects of child sexual exploitation and trafficking offences were identified or arrested.

title: Carreto family — Tenancingo to New York trafficking
who: Carreto family pimping network based in Tenancingo, Tlaxcala
what: From 1991 to 2004 the Carreto family, based in San Miguel de Tenancingo, Tlaxcala, recruited young, poor women and girls in Mexico by deception and forced them into prostitution in brothels in Queens and Brooklyn, using rape, threats and forced abortion. Josue and Gerardo Flores Carreto were sentenced to 50 years each in April 2006 and Daniel Perez Alonso to 25 years. Their mother Consuelo Carreto Valencia was extradited in January 2007 and pleaded guilty to sex trafficking on 22 July 2008.

title: Rendon-Reyes trafficking organization (Tenancingo)
who: Rendon-Reyes Trafficking Organization, Tenancingo, Tlaxcala
what: From December 2004 to November 2015 the Tenancingo-based Rendon-Reyes organization smuggled women and girls from Mexico and Central America into the US, forced them into prostitution and laundered proceeds back to Mexico. In January 2019 five members were sentenced in Brooklyn to between 15 and 25 years; others had pleaded guilty to racketeering and sex trafficking.

title: Marita Verón case — Tucumán brothel network
who: Brothel and trafficking ring in Tucumán province
cover_up: Campaigners and the victim's family's lawyers said police were often paid to protect prostitution rings; trial court acquitted all 13 in 2012.
what: Marita Verón, aged 23, disappeared in Tucumán in 2002, allegedly abducted into forced prostitution. In December 2012 a Tucumán court acquitted all 13 defendants, provoking national protests and calls to impeach the judges. In December 2013 Tucumán's Supreme Court reversed the acquittals and found 10 of the 13 guilty. Her mother's foundation, created in 2008, says it has helped free hundreds of women and girls from brothels. (Verón was an adult; the case is included because it exposed the national network that also trafficked minors.)

title: Netherlands — National Rapporteur estimate of exploited Dutch girls
who: Domestic pimps and 'loverboy' recruiters
what: A report by National Rapporteur Corinne Dettmeijer, prepared with UNODC and published 18 October 2017, estimated that at least 1,320 underage Dutch girls aged 12 to 17 fall victim to sexual exploitation in the Netherlands each year, using 2012–2016 data. Underage girls made up nearly half of female victims in the Dutch sex industry. In October 2025 the current rapporteur reported reported exploitation cases rising from 868 (2023) to 944 (2024), with more teenage victims.

title: Canada — police-reported trafficking 2013–2023 (Ontario hub)
who: Mostly domestic traffickers known to victims
what: Statistics Canada reported on 1 November 2024 that police recorded 4,543 trafficking incidents from 2013 to 2023; about 23% of 3,558 victims were under 18 and 93% were women and girls. Ontario accounted for roughly two-thirds of incidents and Toronto alone for 20%. 91% of victims knew their trafficker and 34% were trafficked by an intimate partner; only 10% of completed adult court cases with a trafficking charge ended in a guilty decision.

title: Melbourne flight attendant jailed for abusing 26 girls in the Philippines
who: Australian travelling offender (airline flight attendant)
what: On 30 March 2020 a 52-year-old Melbourne flight attendant was sentenced in Australia to 18.5 years' imprisonment (14 years non-parole) for sexually abusing 26 girls aged 12 to 17 in the Philippines on 25 occasions between 2010 and 2017. He was prosecuted in Australia under Commonwealth laws covering child sexual offences committed overseas.

title: Sydney man sentenced after rescue of three children in the Philippines
who: Australian offender abusing children in the Philippines
what: A 64-year-old Sydney man was sentenced on 3 December 2021 to eight years and 10 months for sexual activity with children under 16 outside Australia and producing child abuse material overseas, among other charges. The AFP investigation led to three children being removed from harm in the Philippines in May 2020.

title: Sydney man jailed for persistent abuse of a child in the Philippines
who: Australian offender procuring a child in the Philippines
what: On 17 December 2021 a Sydney man was sentenced to nine years and one month for procuring a child to engage in sexual activity outside Australia and persistent sexual abuse of a child outside Australia, plus abuse-material offences. One child was rescued in the Philippines.

title: Brisbane man jailed for abusing children in the Visayas, Philippines
who: Australian offender abusing children in the Philippines
what: A 57-year-old Brisbane man was sentenced on 31 January 2022 to eight years' imprisonment (four non-parole) for abusing children overseas. Five children were rescued in the Visayas region of the Philippines in December 2019 as a result of the investigation.

title: Australia — passport ban for registered child sex offenders (2017)
who: Australian Government
what: Laws taking effect on 13 December 2017 allow Australia to cancel the passports of up to 20,000 registered child sex offenders to stop them travelling to abuse children. The Foreign Minister said about 800 registered offenders travelled overseas in 2016, often to developing countries in Asia, and about 40% did so without notifying police. Reporting at the time said about half of the trips were to Southeast Asia.

title: Philippines blacklists Australian sex offender after AFP warning (2013)
who: Philippine Bureau of Immigration; Australian Federal Police
what: In April 2013 Philippine immigration officers at Manila airport intercepted and blacklisted an Australian convicted in Perth in 2010 of indecent assault on children, travelling on a New Zealand passport and planning to stay in Iloilo, after an Australian police warning that he posed a risk to Filipino children. It is an example of offender travel notifications between countries.

title: Black Axe in Palermo — 14 convicted (2018), 4 acquitted of mafia association (2019)
who: Black Axe (Nigerian confraternity) cell in Palermo
network: Black Axe (Neo-Black Movement of Africa confraternity)
what: A Palermo police operation on 18 November 2016 arrested 19 alleged members of a Black Axe cell based in the Ballarò district; prosecutors said it ran debt collection, exploitation of prostitution and drug trafficking with mafia-style initiation rites. On 21 May 2018 a Palermo judge (fast-track procedure) convicted 14 Nigerians to a combined 87 years. In November 2019 the Palermo Corte d'Assise, trying five others, did not accept the mafia-association charge: four were acquitted and one was jailed for 11 years for kidnapping and sexual violence.

title: IOM: up to 80% of Nigerian women and girls arriving in Italy may be sex-trafficking victims
who: Nigerian trafficking networks via Libya
what: In July 2017 the International Organization for Migration said perhaps 80 per cent of Nigerian migrant women and girls arriving by sea in Italy could be sex-trafficking victims, and that its Italy office had seen an almost 600 per cent rise in potential victims over three years. IOM indicators included age (most victims 13–24) and being 'controlled' by other migrants. Thomson Reuters Foundation later cited IOM data that Nigerian female arrivals rose from 1,500 in 2014 to more than 11,000 in 2016.

title: Oba of Benin revokes trafficking 'juju' oaths (March 2018)
who: Oba of Benin, Ewuare II; Edo traditional priests
what: In March 2018 the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, publicly revoked the curses that juju priests had used to bind trafficking victims to their traffickers and laid a curse on anyone involved in trafficking within his domain. Thomson Reuters Foundation reported in September 2018 that anecdotal evidence suggested trafficking had slowed, and cited UNODC that at least nine in ten Nigerian women trafficked to Europe come from Edo State.

title: Nigeria — cult-linked networks traffic women and girls to Europe and West African mines (US TIP 2025)
who: Nigerian organized trafficking networks, some linked to cult organizations/confraternities
what: The 2025 US Trafficking in Persons report says highly organized groups, sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations or confraternities, recruit and exploit Nigerian women and girls in sex trafficking in Italy, Spain and the UK, and that networks move women and girls to mining regions in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. In the reporting year courts convicted 49 traffickers and the government identified 2,058 victims. It describes corruption and official complicity, including among officials responsible for anti-trafficking, as significant concerns.

title: Libya — sex trafficking of sub-Saharan girls in southern brothels; abuse of transiting children (US TIP 2025)
who: Commercial sex rings; armed groups; officials
cover_up: Observers report systemic official complicity, including Libyan Coast Guard, immigration and security officials; the government has never reported prosecuting or convicting anyone for sex or labour trafficking.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says commercial sex rings subject sub-Saharan women and girls to sex trafficking in brothels, particularly in Ubari, Sabha and Murzuq, and that Nigerian women and girls are at increased risk. It cites an international organization finding that 77 per cent of children and youth transiting Libya experienced indicators of exploitation amounting to trafficking.

title: Michael Pepe — former US Marine jailed 210 years for abusing girls in Cambodia
who: Michael Joseph Pepe (retired US Marine Corps captain)
what: Pepe travelled to Cambodia in 2005, was arrested there in 2006 and charged in the US in 2007. His first conviction was overturned by the Ninth Circuit in 2018; at a retrial in August 2021 victims testified he drugged, bound, beat and raped them, and prosecutors showed homemade abuse material. On 14 February 2022 a Los Angeles federal judge sentenced him to 210 years. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the Cambodian National Police.

title: Ronald Boyajian — 70 years for buying a 9-year-old girl in Svay Pak
who: Ronald Gerard Boyajian (US registered sex offender)
what: Boyajian, a registered sex offender with 1995 California convictions, was arrested in Cambodia in February 2009 on what prosecutors called his 35th trip to Asia over nine years, and was among the first three men expelled to the US under ICE's 'Operation Twisted Traveler' in August 2009. Convicted of illicit sexual conduct with a nine-year-old girl in Svay Pak, he was sentenced on 1 August 2016 to 70 years and ordered to pay $40,000 restitution.

title: Operation Twisted Traveler — ICE crackdown on US offenders in Cambodia (2009)
who: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement; Cambodian police
what: In August 2009 three previously convicted US sex offenders arrested by Cambodian police in February — Ronald Boyajian, Erik Peeters and Jack Sporich — were returned to Los Angeles as the first defendants charged under 'Operation Twisted Traveler'. ICE head John Morton called Cambodia 'ground zero for child sex tourism'; ICE had stationed an agent in Cambodia full-time. Peeters was accused of abusing at least three Cambodian boys and Sporich of abusing a boy in Siem Reap (accusations at the time).

title: Svay Pak child brothels — 2003 raid and later decline
who: Brothels in Svay Pak (mostly ethnic Vietnamese victims)
cover_up: The 22 January 2003 police raid was widely advertised in advance; almost all children had been moved and no pimps or clients were arrested. Local authorities had extorted brothel owners.
what: Svay Pak, a poor fishing village on the outskirts of Phnom Penh, became notorious as a place where foreign men bought sex with children; CNN in 2017 reported girls there being sold by their families. After crackdowns by the government, police and international agencies, open street sales ended and the trade moved to more hidden venues such as massage parlours and karaoke bars. ABC News reported in 2017 that survey estimates of the share of minors among Cambodia's sex workers had fallen from nearly 35% to 1–2%.

title: Cambodia — child sex tourism and brothels; scam compounds (US TIP 2025)
who: Brothel and entertainment operators; foreign and Cambodian offenders
cover_up: The report says official complicity, including at senior levels, inhibited effective law enforcement.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says Cambodian men and men from Australia, South Africa, the United States and other countries in Asia and Europe sexually exploit children in the tourism industry, increasingly via social media; children as young as 13 are exploited in brothels to pay family debts; and women and girls are exploited in online scam compounds.

title: Lake Volta, Ghana — child trafficking in fishing (IJM prevalence study 2023)
who: Fishing-boat owners and intermediaries on Lake Volta
what: A 2023 International Justice Mission household survey of 1,286 children in three fishing districts around Lake Volta estimated that about 37.7 per cent were likely trafficked and a further 45.1 per cent were in likely exploitative child labour. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit children as young as four in Lake Volta's fishing industry, controlling them with violence and limited food, and that girls in the fishing sector are vulnerable to sexual exploitation; it notes observers reported forced child labour on the lake has decreased.

title: Senegal — forced begging and abuse of talibé children in Quranic schools (HRW 2019)
who: Some marabouts (Quranic teachers) running residential daaras
what: Human Rights Watch and the Senegalese PPDH platform reported on 11 June 2019 that over 100,000 talibé children in Senegal are forced by some Quranic teachers to beg daily, often under quotas enforced by beatings. For 2017–2018 they documented 16 deaths of talibés from beatings, neglect or endangerment, 61 cases of beatings, 15 cases of actual or attempted rape or sexual abuse and 14 cases of children chained or imprisoned, in 8 of Senegal's 14 regions. The 2025 US TIP report says the government identified 573 child forced-begging victims in the year.

title: Kédougou, Senegal — sex trafficking of girls at gold-mining sites
who: Trafficking networks supplying mining camps
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit women and girls as young as 12 in sex trafficking throughout Senegal's southeastern gold-mining region of Kédougou; most victims are from Nigeria, with others from Senegal, Mali, Benin, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Guinea, Sierra Leone and China. It also reports some tourists exploit children in Dakar and Saint-Louis, and to a lesser extent Cap Skirring and La Petite Côte.

title: Kenya coast — UNICEF/Government study on child sex tourism (2006)
who: Tourists and local clients in Kenya's beach resorts
what: On 19 December 2006 UNICEF and Kenya's Ministry of Home Affairs launched a joint study of four beach resort areas. It found that up to 30 per cent of 12–18-year-old girls living there were involved in casual sex work and that two to three thousand children were in full-time commercial sex; 38 per cent of clients were Kenyan and 44 per cent Italian, German or Swiss tourists. Vice President Moody Awori accepted the findings and acknowledged police and community failure to enforce the law.

title: Kenya — child sex trafficking in Kilifi/Kwale villas; Karamoja girls to Nairobi (US TIP 2025)
who: Family members, taxi drivers, recruiters; foreign and local offenders
cover_up: The report notes ongoing concerns of official complicity with no reported action against complicit officials.
what: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 NGO study estimating that more than 2,000 children were exploited in child sex trafficking in Kilifi and Kwale counties, increasingly in private villas and vacation homes rather than hotels. It also reports cross-border rings moving women and underage girls from Uganda's Karamoja region to Nairobi, and truck drivers, miners and Lake Victoria fishermen exploiting children.

title: The Gambia — child sex tourism on the Senegambia Strip (US TIP 2025)
who: Organized networks using European and Gambian travel agencies
what: The 2025 US TIP report says European tourists, primarily from the UK, reportedly travel to The Gambia to exploit children, and that organized sex-trafficking networks use European and Gambian travel agencies to promote the country as a destination, especially the Senegambia Strip. Women and girls from other West African countries, especially Nigeria, are recruited for tourism jobs and then sexually exploited. The Tourism Offences Act provides life imprisonment for child trafficking by tourists.

title: Madagascar — child sex tourism and karaoke-bar exploitation (US TIP 2025)
who: Malagasy and foreign offenders
cover_up: The report calls corruption and official complicity significant concerns; one official was investigated.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says most child sex-trafficking victims are exploited by Malagasy men, but foreign tourists, often from France, also exploit children; parents sometimes encourage daughters into commercial sex with tourists, and children are exploited in Antananarivo karaoke bars. Courts convicted 15 traffickers, the first convictions in four years. A Nosy Be anti-trafficking committee exists. In July 2025 police in Nosy Be arrested two women suspected of filming abuse of their own children and selling the videos to foreign buyers via mobile money (charged; L'Express de Madagascar).

title: Morocco — royal pardon of Spanish child rapist Daniel Galván (2013)
who: Daniel Galván Viña
cover_up: King Mohammed VI pardoned Galván on 30 July 2013 among 48 Spanish prisoners; he left Morocco on an expired passport with authorities' knowledge before the pardon was cancelled. Protesters in Rabat were violently dispersed. A 2010 US cable reported a 2006 royal pardon of a French man convicted of abusing a 15-year-old boy in Marrakesh.
what: Daniel Galván Viña, a retired Spanish professor, was arrested in Morocco in December 2010 and in September 2011 sentenced to 30 years for raping 11 Moroccan children aged 4 to 14. In late July 2013 he was among 48 Spanish prisoners pardoned by King Mohammed VI; after protests outside parliament in Rabat, the king revoked the pardon on 4 August 2013, citing the gravity of the crimes and the victims' rights, and said he had not been told the details of the case. Galván had already left Morocco; he was later arrested in Spain.

title: Morocco — foreign offenders in Tangier vacation rentals (US TIP 2025)
who: Foreign nationals, primarily from Europe and the Middle East
what: The 2025 US TIP report says some foreign nationals, primarily from Europe and the Middle East, sexually exploit children in major Moroccan cities, and NGOs report tourists exploit children in Tangier in vacation rentals owned and managed by European nationals. It also reports alleged exploitation of children after the September 2023 Al Haouz earthquake. Courts convicted 60 traffickers in 2024.

title: Tanzania — child sex trafficking in Zanzibar and cities (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers, brokers, foster families
cover_up: The report says the government did not adequately address corruption and official complicity.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit children in sex trafficking, including by foreign offenders ('extraterritorial sexual exploitation'), and in forced labour and domestic servitude in Zanzibar, and that women and girls from the mainland are brought to Zanzibar with false promises. Child sex trafficking also occurs in Arusha, Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Mbeya and Mwanza.

title: Uganda — Karamojong children sold at border markets (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers including community 'elders'
what: The 2025 US TIP report says NGOs estimate the majority of child sex-trafficking victims in Uganda are ethnically Karamojong, especially from Napak district. Traffickers, sometimes community 'elders', force children to meet them at international borders, where markets are organized to sell children into domestic servitude or sex trafficking. Women, girls and boys are exploited in Kampala brothels, bars and homes.

title: Malawi — Dzaleka refugee camp girls recruited for sex trafficking (US TIP 2025)
who: Transnational crime syndicates operating from bars and compounds in the camp
cover_up: The report says official complicity continued to impede enforcement.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says organized transnational syndicates operating from informal bars and housing in Dzaleka camp (about 53,000 refugees in a space for 10,000) recruit girls for sex trafficking inside the camp and in roadside bars along the highway to Lilongwe; the camp is a waypoint on the 'Southern Route' to South Africa. Girls are also exploited in bars and illegal brothels in Lilongwe and Blantyre.

title: Mozambique — girls exploited along the Maputo–South Africa highway and at mines (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers at rest stops, bars, mining areas; non-state armed groups
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit girls in rest stops, bars and restaurants along the Maputo–South Africa highway and around mines, and that non-state armed groups abducted children and sexually exploited girls. Girls as young as 11 working as nannies are vulnerable when employment ends.

title: Zimbabwe — sex trafficking around gold and diamond mines; girls traded under ngozi (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers at mining sites; families
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit women and children in sex trafficking around mines, sometimes for money or food, and may exploit children as panners and ore couriers in gold and diamond mines. Traditional practices including trading daughters for food or money and ngozi — giving a relative to another family to atone for a killing — make girls vulnerable. Low-level official complicity persisted.

title: DR Congo — forced labour and sexual exploitation of children at eastern artisanal mines (US TIP 2025)
who: Mining bosses, miners, family members, government officials, armed groups
cover_up: Traffickers named in the report include government officials; corruption and complicity contributed to impunity.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says mining bosses, other miners, family members, government officials and armed groups force or coerce adults and children into forced labour in artisanal mines in eastern DRC, including through debt bondage, and that most trafficking is internal, including sex trafficking and forced marriage of girls.

title: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana — 1.56 million children in cocoa child labour (NORC 2020)
who: Cocoa supply chain (farms supplying international chocolate companies)
what: A US Department of Labor-funded study by NORC at the University of Chicago, released 19 October 2020, estimated 1.56 million children were in cocoa-related child labour in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana in 2018–19, 95 per cent in hazardous work, and found child labour had increased since 2008–09 while production rose. Industry had committed in the 2001 Harkin-Engel Protocol and a 2010 declaration to cut the worst forms by 70 per cent by 2020. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Ghanaian and other West African children in forced labour in cocoa.

title: Côte d'Ivoire — girls brought to Abidjan for domestic servitude; Nigerian girls at mines (US TIP 2025)
who: Relatives and Nigerian trafficking networks
what: The 2025 US TIP report says distant relatives bring girls from rural Côte d'Ivoire and other West African countries to Abidjan for school or training and then exploit them in domestic servitude, where they are vulnerable to sexual exploitation; Ivorian women and girls are sex-trafficked especially in Abidjan; and Nigerian traffickers recruit women and girls for shop jobs then exploit them in gold-mining and cocoa regions.

title: South Africa — rural children trafficked to Gauteng and Western Cape (US TIP 2025)
who: Brothel owners and traffickers; some parents
cover_up: Low-level official corruption and complicity persisted.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit victims from rural areas, especially children, and exploit them in sex trafficking in cities, especially Gauteng and Western Cape; brothel owners use drugs to control victims including children; and some parents exploit their children in sex trafficking or online sexual exploitation for money or drugs.

title: Ethiopia — girls trafficked to Djibouti, Sudan and Saudi Arabia (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers and begging rings
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Ethiopian women and children in forced begging, sometimes via organized begging rings, in Saudi Arabia, and exploit Ethiopian girls in domestic servitude and sex trafficking in neighbouring countries, particularly Djibouti and Sudan, sometimes using drugs for control. Reports of official complicity continued.

title: Nepal → India — trafficking of girls to Indian brothels (estimates)
who: Trafficking networks recruiting via false job, marriage and online romance offers
cover_up: US TIP 2025: serious concerns of official complicity; traffickers bribe some Indian officials to fly Nepali workers to third countries.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers use job offers and online romance scams to recruit Nepali women and children to India for sex trafficking; Nepali courts convicted 406 traffickers (231 for sex trafficking) in the year. A 2024 study it cites found a majority of workers in Nepal's adult entertainment sector were sex-trafficking victims, nearly half of them children. Research collated on Wikipedia gives estimates of 5,000–10,000 Nepali women and girls trafficked to India each year across a 1,850 km open border.

title: Kolkata red-light areas — rescues of trafficked Nepali girls and minors (2015, 2025)
who: Brothel keepers and traffickers in Kolkata
what: In January 2015 police, with International Justice Mission and three NGOs, freed six young women trafficked from Nepal from four brothels in Kolkata's largest red-light area; all had fake adult ID documents, which IJM said traffickers issue to underage girls. On 10 September 2025 Kolkata Police's Anti-Human Trafficking Unit rescued ten people including nine minor girls from a house in Burtolla, North Kolkata, and arrested six people, including the couple running it (charged). The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit significant numbers of Nepali and Bangladeshi women and girls for sex trafficking in India.

title: Kamathipura, Mumbai — red-light district fed by trafficking from Nepal and Indian states
who: Brothels of Kamathipura
what: Kamathipura, Mumbai's oldest and largest red-light district and one of Asia's largest, was established over 150 years ago under British rule; the BBC in 2013 put its sex workers at an estimated 20,000. Girls were trafficked there from poor villages in other Indian states, some as young as 11, on promises of domestic work. The 2025 US Trafficking in Persons report is cited, though it could not be opened for this map, for a shift of sex trafficking in India toward spas, hotels and private residences, and for 2022 crime-data figures of 204 convicted traffickers and 1,134 acquittals; that report could not be opened in this pass (state.gov blocked).

title: Bangladesh — girls trafficked to India, Pakistan and the Gulf; Rohingya girls near Cox's Bazar (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers, recruitment agents, armed groups in Rohingya camps
cover_up: Corruption and official complicity were significant concerns; corrupt policing in Rohingya camps.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bangladeshi women and girls in sex trafficking abroad, including in India, Pakistan and Gulf countries, and observers estimate children are 40 per cent of Bangladeshi sex-trafficking victims exploited abroad. Tourists have increased demand for sexual exploitation, including of Rohingya girls, near Cox's Bazar, where more than one million Rohingya refugees live in 33 camps. Courts convicted 103 traffickers, down from 407.

title: Pakistan → China — 629 girls and women sold as 'brides' (AP 2019)
who: Brokers selling poor (often Christian) Pakistani girls and women to Chinese men
cover_up: Officials told AP the investigation largely stopped after June 2019 because of pressure from government officials fearful of harming ties with Beijing; in October 2019 a Faisalabad court acquitted 31 Chinese nationals after witnesses were threatened or bribed into silence.
what: AP obtained a list compiled by Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency of 629 girls and women sold as brides to Chinese men from 2018 to mid-2019. In October 2019 a court in Faisalabad acquitted 31 Chinese nationals charged in the biggest case. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers target impoverished Christian communities to send women and girls to China, where hundreds reported being forced into commercial sex.

title: Myanmar → China — Kachin women and girls sold as 'brides' (HRW 2019)
who: Traffickers including relatives and acquaintances; buying families in China
cover_up: HRW said Myanmar and Chinese authorities were 'looking away'; police on both sides gave traffickers little reason to fear enforcement.
what: Human Rights Watch's 112-page report of 21 March 2019 documented women and girls from Kachin and northern Shan States, many displaced by conflict, sold for US$3,000–13,000 to Chinese families, locked up and raped so they would become pregnant. One survivor was trafficked at 16 by her sister-in-law. The 2025 US TIP report says displaced women and girls in Kachin and Shan remain vulnerable to forced marriage and forced childbearing in China.

title: Vietnam and Laos → China — girls sold as brides (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers and marriage brokers
what: The 2025 US TIP reports say traffickers in Vietnamese border villages lure women and girls, particularly Hmong, to China for forced marriages involving sex trafficking or forced labour, and use 'bride kidnapping' to exploit ethnic-minority girls in the northwest highlands; in Laos, traffickers increasingly kidnap or recruit women and girls via marriage brokers to China for sex trafficking, forced labour and forced surrogacy. Vietnam identified 236 child victims in 2024.

title: Swiss bar owner jailed 16 years for abusing more than 80 boys in Pattaya and northern Thailand
who: Unnamed Swiss national (72, from Lucerne) who ran a bar in Pattaya
what: A Swiss man previously convicted of abusing children in Fribourg (1980) and Valais (1991) returned to Thailand in 1996 and, mainly in 2002–2013, abused more than 80 boys in Pattaya, where he ran a bar with a hotel room frequented by Europeans, and in Nong Hoi in the north; he also forced boys to perform acts with European clients. Charged in Fribourg with human trafficking, encouraging prostitution, sexual acts with children and abuse material, he was sentenced by a Swiss court on 1 March 2018 to 16 years.

title: Mark Frost — 13 life terms for abuse of boys in Thailand and the UK (2017)
who: Mark Frost (also known as Andrew Tracey), former teacher and scout leader
what: Frost, who had held positions of trust in UK schools and scouting and first admitted an offence in 1992, abused boys from poor families in Thailand in 2011–2013, including streaming abuse by webcam to another European man. In February 2017 he was sentenced to 13 terms of life imprisonment after pleading guilty to 45 offences against boys in the UK and Thailand. The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse cited the case as one of only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad. Eight Thai boys secured civil compensation in 2018.

title: Patong, Phuket — foreign bar owner sentenced to 1,073 years after raid freed six minors (2024)
who: Illegal bar on Bangla Road
cover_up: Five senior Patong police officers were transferred after the raid; the foreign owner initially fled to a neighbouring country.
what: A 2023 raid on an illegal bar on Bangla Road, Patong, rescued six victims of child sexual exploitation under 18. On 19 July 2024 the Phuket Provincial Court sentenced seven defendants, Thai and foreign; the prime defendant, a foreign owner, received a total of 1,073 years. Five senior Patong police were transferred after the raid. The 2025 US TIP report says children from Thailand, Burma, Cambodia and Laos are increasingly sex-trafficked in brothels, bars, karaoke lounges and hotels.

title: David Timothy Deakin — life sentence, Angeles City court (2020)
who: David Timothy Deakin (US national)
what: Acting on an FBI referral, the Philippine National Bureau of Investigation arrested US national David Timothy Deakin in Mabalacat, Pampanga, in 2017, rescuing two girls and seizing hard drives of abuse material; IJM said he abused Filipino children, recorded it and sold it online to foreign customers. In May 2020 the Angeles City Regional Trial Court Branch 58 convicted him of large-scale human trafficking and sentenced him to life imprisonment, in the country's first conviction delivered by videoconference. The 2025 US TIP report names Angeles City among tourist destinations with high demand for commercial sex.

title: Philippines — foreign offenders and child sex trafficking in tourist towns (US TIP 2025)
who: Foreign offenders; family members; brothel and bar operators
cover_up: Corruption and official complicity remained significant concerns.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says sex trafficking frequently occurs in tourist destinations such as Boracay, Angeles City, Olongapo, Puerto Galera and Surigao. Many foreign offenders are convicted or charged sex offenders at home, most commonly from Australia, Japan, New Zealand, the UK and the US, with more reports from Canada, Morocco, Iraq and Denmark. Courts convicted 143 traffickers, 120 for sex trafficking.

title: Indonesia — child sexual exploitation in the Riau Islands and 'contract marriages' in Puncak (US TIP 2025)
who: Foreign offenders; brokers of 'contract marriages'
cover_up: The report says the government tacitly accepted 'contract marriages'; corruption and complicity significantly impeded efforts.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says extraterritorial child sexual exploitation is prevalent in the Riau Islands bordering Singapore, and women and girls are coerced into commercial sex notably in Batam. It also reports that Middle Eastern tourists pay more than $700 for week-long 'contract marriages' in Puncak, Bogor, involving girls as young as nine, a practice the government tacitly accepted. In October 2017 Batam police arrested a Singaporean man accused of molesting three boys (IBTimes, charged).

title: Japan — 'JK business' and compensated dating (police survey 2024; US TIP 2025)
who: JK businesses, often with organized-crime ties
what: The 'JK business' sells simulated dates and services with high-school girls. A National Police Agency survey at the end of December 2024 counted 91 establishments advertising in this way, 70 per cent in Tokyo. Kanagawa first regulated it in 2011 and Tokyo enacted a dedicated ordinance in 2017. The 2025 US TIP report says JK variants and 'compensated dating', often tied to organized crime, continue to facilitate sex trafficking of Japanese children and of children from China, South Korea, Laos, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam.

title: South Korea — runaway children in commercial sex; police officer convicted (US TIP 2025)
who: Entertainment establishments, escort services, chat-room operators
cover_up: NGOs previously reported some local police sexually exploited children; one officer was convicted (bribery, secrecy violations) and another acquitted.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit South Korean women and children, including runaways, in bars, nightclubs and internet-advertised escort services, and chat-room operators coerce children with compromising images into producing sexual material. A court convicted a local police officer in a 2022 case involving alleged complicity in trafficking-related crimes and sentenced him to five years; another officer was acquitted.

title: Mongolia — girls sex-trafficked in Ulaanbaatar hotels and karaoke bars (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers in hotels, massage parlours, karaoke clubs
cover_up: The report says exploitation is sometimes facilitated by lack of police enforcement; some families are complicit.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls are sex-trafficked in Mongolian hotels, massage parlours, illegal brothels, bars and karaoke clubs, mostly in Ulaanbaatar, provincial centres and border areas, sometimes facilitated by a lack of police enforcement; traffickers use online platforms to groom and blackmail children; and children taken abroad for competitions have instead been put to work, e.g. as horse jockeys.

title: Sri Lanka — child sex tourism in coastal areas (US TIP 2025)
who: Foreign and local offenders
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers reportedly exploit boys and girls in child sex trafficking, including in coastal areas, for foreign offenders, and recommends investigating complicit establishments. The government convicted six traffickers and identified seven child victims in the year.

title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan — girls lured to cities; children in institutions (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers recruiting via social media
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers lure girls and women from rural Kazakhstan and neighbouring Central Asian, East Asian and Eastern European countries with job offers as waitresses, models or nannies in large cities, and exploit Kazakh women and girls in Russia, Uzbekistan, the Middle East, Europe, East Asia and the US. In Uzbekistan, children in institutions are vulnerable to sex trafficking.

title: Medellín — US federal prosecutions of travelling offenders (10 convictions by May 2026)
who: US-national travelling offenders; HSI Colombia; Alcaldía de Medellín
what: BluRadio reported on 21 May 2026 that US courts, working with Colombian authorities and the Medellín mayor's office, had handed down a tenth sentence in an offensive against foreigners exploiting children in Medellín: Ramón Arellano Sandoval, 65, sentenced in Miami to 30 years for attempted sexual exploitation of a 14-year-old Medellín girl, who had entered the city 48 times in two years. On 22 January 2026 Manuel Poceiro, 69, of Miami, was sentenced to life for travelling to Colombia to exploit minors, after HSI found material involving at least five minors. In March 2024 US national Timothy Alan Livingston was found in a Medellín hotel with two minors (aged between 12 and 16, per police sources); a Colombian judge issued an arrest warrant and Interpol a blue notice (charged, at large at the time).

title: Cartagena — 'La Madame' network exploiting girls for tourists (plea 2018)
who: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ('La Madame')
cover_up: At hearings she threatened to reveal the names of politicians and powerful men she said were clients (her claim, unverified).
what: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ran a sex network from a Bocagrande apartment in Cartagena, supplying young women and minors to parties on yachts, in hotels and at beaches and sending women to Panama, Mexico, Miami and the Bahamas; prosecutors seized 15 ledgers of clients and payments, and a WhatsApp group listed 200 women. In 2018 she accepted charges of human trafficking and conspiracy in a plea deal and was sentenced to eight years and one month; she was released on parole in 2023. US ICE supported the investigation.

title: Colombia — Tren de Aragua sex trafficking of Venezuelan girls; webcam industry (US TIP 2025)
who: Tren de Aragua; ELN; webcam studios
cover_up: Two complicit officials received plea-deal sentences of 7.5 years, below the statutory minimum.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says Tren de Aragua and the ELN run sex-trafficking networks in Villa del Rosario, Norte de Santander, and Tren de Aragua uses Cúcuta's transport hub to move victims to Argentina, Ecuador and Peru and operates in Bogotá, Cali, Medellín and Pereira. Traffickers recruit women and girls, mostly Colombians and displaced Venezuelans, into 'webcam modelling', an industry likely worth over $1.2 billion a year. Sex trafficking of girls is prevalent in tourist areas and extractive zones.

title: Sosúa — 29 trafficking victims including 20 minors freed in US–Dominican sting (2015)
who: Local pimping ring in a tourist town
what: In April 2015 Dominican authorities, with HSI Santo Domingo and two private US organisations, lured alleged traffickers to a staged 'sex party' in the tourist town of Sosúa, freeing 29 victims including 20 minors aged 14–17 and arresting seven Dominican nationals (two women, five men), who faced up to 15 years. The 2025 US TIP report says teenage girls are frequently exploited on streets, in parks and on beaches, and NGOs link rising child victim numbers to weak regulation of tourism.

title: Troy Brimm — 34 years for travelling to Puerto Plata to abuse boys (2013)
who: Troy Douglas Brimm, of Modesto, California
what: Brimm, 50, was convicted on two counts of travelling to Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic, to engage in illicit sexual conduct with minor boys, including shoe-shine boys, after a flight on 20 October 2009. On 10 January 2013 a Miami federal judge sentenced him to 34 years followed by lifetime supervised release. The case was investigated by HSI Miami with the Dominican National Police and the Puerto Plata Prosecutor's Office.

title: La Pampa, Madre de Dios — Operación Mercurio 2019 and sex trafficking in mining camps
who: Bar/brothel networks serving illegal gold-mining camps
what: On 19–20 February 2019 more than 1,500 military and police began Operación Mercurio against illegal gold mining in La Pampa, in the Tambopata reserve buffer zone, under a state of emergency. Peru's Women's Minister said the worst crimes, including child sexual exploitation and child labour, had been committed there, and her ministry took in minors and women rescued from trafficking. Reporting in 2022 said police were still dismantling networks recruiting women to La Pampa bars; a 16-year-old girl previously rescued from a La Pampa trafficking band was found murdered at km 108 in April 2021.

title: Peru — foreign tourists exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Amazon (US TIP 2025)
who: Criminal groups transporting tourists on the Amazon
cover_up: Authorities charged two police officers for crimes against trafficking victims; corruption remained a significant concern.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says tourists from the US and Europe exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Peruvian Amazon, and in Loreto criminal groups take foreign tourists by boat to remote venues on the Amazon River where women and children are exploited. Peruvian, Venezuelan and Bolivian women and girls are lured to mining and logging camps. Courts convicted 59 traffickers in 2024.

title: Brazil — Federal Highway Police 'Projeto Mapear' of child sexual exploitation points on highways
who: Truck stops, bars, motels along federal highways
what: Brazil's Federal Highway Police (PRF) and Childhood Brasil have mapped roadside sites vulnerable to child sexual exploitation for about 19 years. The 2021–2022 survey, released 31 May 2023, assessed more than 9,700 points, rating 640 critical and about 1,800 high-risk; the worst conditions were on BR-116 (12 critical points), BR-153, BR-101, BR-163, BR-232 and BR-040. An earlier edition found 69% of victims female and 22% transgender, and 38% from elsewhere, possibly trafficked. The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking is common along BR-386, BR-116 and BR-255.

title: Brazil — child sex tourism in northeastern coastal cities (Fortaleza, Natal, Recife, Salvador)
who: Taxi drivers, hotel and bar staff facilitating foreign offenders
cover_up: US TIP 2025: no investigations of complicit officials reported; a 2016 child sex-trafficking case involving an elected official in Paraná unresolved.
what: In 2006 Brazil's Federal Police described sex tourism as most frequent in Fortaleza, Recife, Salvador and Natal, and ran periodic raids, e.g. on a Ponta Negra (Natal) nightclub with 110 foreigners (no children found that night). The 2025 US TIP report says taxi drivers and hotel, bar and nightclub staff in coastal tourist destinations facilitate child sex trafficking, and cites a study suggesting up to 16 per cent of girls aged 14–17 in one northeastern metropolitan area were likely victims of commercial sexual exploitation.

title: Bolivia — foreign offenders in Indigenous communities near Rurrenabaque (US TIP 2025)
who: Foreign offenders; parents; online abuse-material producers
what: The 2025 US TIP report says foreign offenders exploited children in rural Indigenous communities in northern La Paz department, in and around Rurrenabaque and Santa Cruz, and in tourist areas of La Paz and Beni; production of abuse material for sale online is rising in Cochabamba, El Alto and Santa Cruz; and Bolivian women and girls are exploited in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Panama and Peru. Tren de Aragua is reported to be involved in trafficking in Bolivia.

title: Paraguay — 47,000 children in criadazgo domestic servitude (US TIP 2025)
who: Families taking in children as unpaid domestic workers
what: The 2025 US TIP report says criadazgo — compelling children to work as domestic workers — is a common form of trafficking in Paraguay; an estimated 47,000 children are in criadazgo, mostly girls (boys are 30 per cent), and many are highly vulnerable to sex and labour trafficking. Colombia's report describes the same practice.

title: Haiti — restavek child domestic servitude and gang exploitation of children (US TIP 2025)
who: Host families (restavek); armed gangs
cover_up: Observers report police and immigration officials complicit at the Haiti–Dominican Republic border.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says a large share of Haiti's trafficking cases involve children in restavek domestic servitude, often physically abused and unpaid, and that displacement from Port-au-Prince increased children's risk of sexual exploitation in the restavek system. Gangs exploit women and girls in sex trafficking; an international organization reported close to 50 per cent of gang members are children, with a 70 per cent rise in child recruitment in 2024.

title: Jamaica — child sex trafficking in resort towns; 6.3% of 12–17-year-olds (US TIP 2025)
who: Family members, 'dons', foreign and local buyers
cover_up: Endemic corruption and official complicity, including within law enforcement, remained significant concerns.
what: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 prevalence study estimating 6.3 per cent of Jamaican children aged 12–17 had experienced conditions indicative of trafficking. Children are subjected to sex trafficking in resort areas frequented by tourists, sometimes with parental involvement, and men pay girls or their families for sex in some communities.

title: Costa Rica — child sex trafficking on Pacific coast and borders (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers in coastal tourist zones
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers subject Costa Rican women and children to sex trafficking, especially in Pacific coastal zones and near the northern and southern borders, where social tolerance increases children's vulnerability; girls from Nicaragua, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela are also identified as victims.

title: Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala — gangs exploit girls; North American offenders (US TIP 2025)
who: Gangs and criminal organizations; foreign offenders
what: The 2025 US TIP reports say criminal organizations including gangs exploit girls in sex trafficking in urban Honduras and Guatemala, and that men from Canada and the US exploit Honduran children. In El Salvador, foreign tourists sexually exploit children and the rapid growth of tourism has created new risks; an estimated 140,000–200,000 Salvadoran children have a parent abroad or detained. Guatemalan children are exploited in Mexico and the US and in live-streamed abuse.

title: Europol: at least 10,000 unaccompanied migrant children missing in Europe (2016)
who: Europol; organized crime exploiting the migrant flow
what: On 31 January 2016 Europol's chief of staff Brian Donald told The Observer that at least 10,000 unaccompanied children had disappeared after arriving in Europe, 5,000 of them in Italy and 1,000 in Sweden, and that Europol had evidence some had been sexually exploited. He said an entire criminal infrastructure had developed over 18 months around exploiting the migrant flow, with many arrests in Germany and Hungary. Save the Children estimated 26,000 unaccompanied children arrived in 2015.

title: Romania–UK 'loverboy' network dismantled — 21 arrested (Eurojust, 2020)
who: Romanian organized criminal group using the 'loverboy' method
what: On 9 September 2020 a Romanian–UK Joint Investigation Team supported by Eurojust arrested 21 members of a hierarchical group active since 2009 that seduced vulnerable Romanian girls with false promises of relationships, exploited minors in prostitution in Romania until they turned 18, and then moved them to the UK, Ireland and Germany. Thirty-two house searches were carried out (23 in Romania, 9 in the UK). Eurojust said Romania and the UK had cooperated in 76 trafficking investigations in four years.

title: Galați/Brăila — 'loverboy' ring exploiting minors in Western Europe (2021)
who: Four suspects detained by DIICOT/BCCO
what: In February 2021 Romanian organised-crime police and DIICOT prosecutors searched eight addresses in Galați and Brăila and detained four suspects for human trafficking, trafficking of minors and pimping. Investigators said that from August 2013 the group recruited girls and young women by the 'loverboy' method, hid minors in intermediate lodgings until they turned 18, then exploited them in Western Europe, earning about €350,000; nine victims, minor and adult, had been identified.

title: Romania — girls in state institutions at risk; victims sent across Europe (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers; staff of some government-run institutions
cover_up: Alleged complicity, misconduct and negligence by government employees in cases involving children in government-run homes remained a concern.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says most identified victims are women and girls exploited in Romania and in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK; children in government-run institutions, particularly girls in homes for persons with disabilities, are at risk of sex trafficking; and Roma children as young as 11 are 'sold' into marriage. Courts convicted 161 traffickers (143 for sex trafficking) and 600 victims were identified in 2024.

title: Bulgaria — girls trafficked to Western Europe; exploitation in state institutions (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers; Roma forced marriages to third-country nationals
cover_up: Corruption in law enforcement and the judiciary and impunity for complicit officials were pervasive; 34 convicted traffickers received suspended sentences.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bulgarian women and girls in sex trafficking throughout Western Europe and in Sofia, resort areas and border towns, and cites a UN special rapporteur finding that child sexual exploitation, including potential sex trafficking, was prevalent among children in government-run institutions. Courts convicted 31 traffickers; only eight received custodial sentences.

title: Moldova — children recruited online; institution leavers at risk (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers using social media and fake job ads
cover_up: A former police officer was convicted of labour trafficking (20 years); corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers increasingly use social media and video chat to recruit children through fake job ads and exploit them in commercial sex, use abuse material as a grooming method, and target children in or leaving state institutions. Courts convicted 33 traffickers (22 for sex trafficking) in 2024.

title: Ukraine — wartime risk to evacuated institutional children; officials allegedly complicit (US TIP 2025)
who: Criminal networks; some institution officials
cover_up: Officials of several state-run residential institutions were allegedly complicit or negligent in trafficking of children in their care; no complicit officials convicted for the eighth year running.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking in Ukraine is underreported and criminals are trying to build online networks to exploit Ukrainian children internationally; children evacuated from at least 195 facilities, including those with disabilities, are at high risk; and Ukrainian refugee women and children are vulnerable in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria and the UK. Ukraine convicted 24 traffickers in 2024, only six with prison terms.

title: Albania — children exploited in tourist season; first trafficking convictions since 2021 (US TIP 2025)
who: Traffickers; families
what: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Albanian women and children in sex trafficking and forced labour, especially in tourist season; Roma and Balkan-Egyptian children are forced to beg; and Albanian migrants in Western Europe, particularly the UK, are vulnerable to forced criminality. Courts convicted two sex traffickers and two labour traffickers, the first convictions since 2021. In the UK, Albanians were the second most common nationality referred as potential victims in 2024 (2,492), 95 per cent as adults.

title: UK — 5,999 child potential victims referred to the National Referral Mechanism (2024)
who: Home Office (NRM)
what: Home Office statistics show 19,125 potential victims of modern slavery referred in 2024, 31 per cent (5,999) children; 78 per cent of child referrals were boys and criminal exploitation was the most common type (48 per cent). UK nationals were 23 per cent of all referrals, three-quarters of them children; Vietnamese nationals were 11 per cent, 416 of them children. In 2017 the Times reported more than 150 Vietnamese minors had gone missing from UK care since 2015.

title: France — 10,000–15,000 French teenagers in child sex trafficking (NGO estimate, US TIP 2025)
who: Small networks of young French men using romance schemes
what: The 2025 US TIP report cites NGO estimates that 10,000 to 15,000 French teenagers are victims of child sex trafficking, says authorities estimate more than half of all trafficking victims in France are French girls and young women exploited by small 'romance' networks, and that traffickers recruit girls in government-funded shelters. Criminal networks force children, mostly from Romania and North Africa, to commit crimes.

title: Germany, Spain, Italy, Greece — romance-method pimps, Nigerian networks, unaccompanied children (US TIP 2025)
who: 'Loverboy' traffickers; Nigerian cult-linked groups; Eastern European recruiters
what: The 2025 US TIP reports say young male traffickers in Germany and Spain coerce girls into sex trafficking through sham romantic relationships; highly organized groups sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations exploit Nigerian women and girls in Germany and Italy, in Italy through debt and 'voodoo' rituals; Eastern European girls are recruited online for child sex trafficking in Italy; and in Greece unaccompanied children are vulnerable to sex trafficking and Roma children from Albania, Bulgaria and Romania are forced to beg.

title: Lebanon — Chez Maurice and Silver-B: about 75 Syrian women freed from sex-trafficking ring (2016)
who: Chez Maurice and Silver-B brothels
cover_up: Chez Maurice was raided in late 2011 when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found trapped there, closed for about three months and reopened. A survivor told Legal Agenda a trafficker claimed he had 'bought the state'.
what: In March 2016 Lebanese security forces freed as many as 75 Syrian women from two brothels, Chez Maurice and Silver-B, in the Maameltein red-light district of Jounieh, and arrested and indicted over a dozen people on sex-trafficking charges. HRW said Syrian refugee women were at particular risk and that the same premises had been raided in 2011, when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found, and later reopened. Lebanon's police identified 87 trafficking victims in 2016, mainly these survivors.

title: Jordan and Türkiye — Syrian refugee girls in forced marriages and sex trafficking (US TIP 2025)
who: Families and brokers arranging unofficial marriages
cover_up: Türkiye: no investigations of complicit officials reported, though corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says Syrian girls in Türkiye — which hosted about 2.9 million displaced Syrians — are forced into marriages in unofficial religious ceremonies, particularly in poor rural regions, and then subjected to domestic servitude and sex trafficking. In Jordan, Syrian refugee women and girls have been sold into forced marriages, and in 2022 authorities investigated a mother for allegedly exploiting her two daughters with foreign tourists.

title: Iraq — officials allegedly coerce ISIS-affiliated families, including children, into sex (US TIP 2025)
who: Security and military officials (alleged, per an international organization); criminal gangs
cover_up: An international organization reported in 2024 that officials coerce family members of detained children into sex acts in exchange for security clearances or civil documents; the government reported no action on official complicity.
what: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls in IDP camps whose relatives have alleged ISIS ties may face sexual exploitation and sex trafficking by security and military officials, and that some officials allegedly exploit such families, including children, in exchange for documents. Criminal gangs reportedly exploit Syrian women and girls at pilgrimage sites, and Yezidi survivors remain at risk of re-trafficking.

title: US Angel Watch Center — 10,000+ notifications to foreign countries on travelling sex offenders
who: US Homeland Security Investigations; CBP; US Marshals Service
what: Under International Megan's Law (signed 2016), the Angel Watch Center notifies foreign governments when US registered child sex offenders plan to travel. DHS says that since 2016 it has made more than 10,000 notifications to foreign countries and notified the State Department of more than 3,500 passports carrying a sex-offender endorsement. HSI child-exploitation arrests rose to 3,771 in 2019 (ABC7, at the centre's ribbon-cutting).

title: UK — IICSA finds gaps let known offenders abuse children abroad (2020)
who: UK Home Office, police, courts
cover_up: IICSA found travel restrictions were rarely used: 11 of 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders in 2017/18 and six Sexual Risk Orders in force in March 2019.
what: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse report on the protection of children outside the UK (January 2020) found that only 11 of the 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders made in 2017/18 included foreign-travel restrictions, that 361 UK nationals sought consular help after arrest abroad for child sex offences in 2013–2017, and that there appear to have been only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad, including Keith Morris (18.5 years, Kenya) and Mark Frost (Thailand).

title: ECPAT 'Offenders on the Move' — Global Study on Sexual Exploitation of Children in Travel and Tourism (2016)
who: ECPAT International and partners (High-Level Task Force chaired by Najat Maalla M'jid)
