what: Published 12 May 2016 after two years' work, the study found sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism had grown despite 20 years of effort, as international arrivals rose from 527 million to 1.135 billion a year. It found there is no typical offender: most are domestic or regional travellers and 'situational' offenders rather than Western paedophiles; the internet has opened new pathways; and conviction rates are alarmingly low. It identified the US and Canada as source countries for offenders and Europe as a source, with exploitation rising in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Peter Dalglish — former UN official jailed 9 years in Nepal for abusing two boys (2019)
who: Peter John Dalglish (Canadian humanitarian, founder of Street Kids International)
what: Nepal Police's Central Investigation Bureau arrested Dalglish, a Canadian who had worked for UN agencies including as a child-labour adviser in Nepal in 2002, at his home in Kavre on 7 April 2018, where boys aged 12 and 14 were found. On 8 July 2019 the Kavre District Court sentenced him to nine years and ordered compensation of Rs 500,000 to each boy. He denied the charges and said he would appeal. Al Jazeera reported fears that foreign offenders were using aid work or philanthropy as cover in Nepal.

title: Fr Nicolás Aguilar Rivera — Puebla diocese priest in Los Angeles
who: Archdiocese of Los Angeles; Diocese of Tehuacán (Mexico)
cover_up: Plaintiffs' attorneys produced a 1988 letter from the Bishop of Tehuacán saying he had warned Cardinal Mahony in 1987 about the priest; the archdiocese denied receiving the warning. The priest fled to Mexico after being relieved of duties and was never arrested.
what: A visiting Mexican priest was assigned to two Los Angeles parishes in 1987. A 1988 police report says he abused 26 grade-school children between March 1987 and January 1988, many recruited as altar servers. A parent reported abuse to a pastor on 8 January 1988; he was removed the next day, charged with 19 felony counts of lewd acts on a child, but fled to Mexico before arrest. As of 2004 the case remained open.

title: Fr Joseph Jeyapaul — Indian priest extradited to Minnesota
who: Diocese of Crookston, Minnesota; diocese in India
cover_up: The Vatican recommended his removal from the priesthood, but the Indian bishop instead imposed a year in a monastery through a canonical trial, and he continued as a priest in India.
what: An Indian priest serving in the Diocese of Crookston in 2004–2005 was removed from ministry in September 2005 and returned to India. He was charged in 2006 with raping a girl from age 14; extradition took about five years after an Interpol alert, with arrest in Erode, India in 2012 and return to Minnesota in November 2014. In 2015 he pleaded guilty to criminal sexual misconduct involving a teenage girl and was sentenced to a year and a day (time served); the rape charges were dismissed under the plea deal and he faced deportation to India.

title: Joseph Henn — Salvatorian priest, fugitive in Rome, extradited 2019
who: Society of the Divine Saviour (Salvatorians); Diocese of Phoenix
cover_up: After his 2003 indictment he fled to Italy; Italy's top court confirmed extradition after his 2005 arrest there, but he disappeared before it could be carried out, remaining a fugitive until May 2019.
what: Henn served at St Mark Parish in Phoenix from 1978 to 1982 and was accused of molesting at least three boys under 15 between 1979 and 1981. Maricopa County indicted him on 13 child-molestation counts in 2003. He was expelled from his order and removed from the priesthood in 2006. Italian police arrested him in Rome on 28 May 2019; U.S. marshals returned him and he was arraigned in Phoenix on 14 June 2019.

title: Fr Johannes Rivoire — Oblate in Nunavut, never extradited from France
who: Oblates of Mary Immaculate (OMI Lacombe Canada; Oblates of France)
cover_up: He left for France in January 1993; a Canadian arrest warrant followed in 1998 and charges were later stayed. A 2022 warrant led to an extradition request that French authorities denied. The 2024 Denis review found the RCMP never contacted the Oblates when charges were laid. In February 2024 the Vatican ruled against his dismissal. He died in France in 2024 without trial.
what: French Oblate Johannes Rivoire worked in the Canadian North from 1959 to 1993. He faced at least three sexual-abuse charges (1998 warrant) concerning Inuit children in Arviat, Rankin Inlet and Naujaat, and a 2022 warrant for indecent assault on a girl in Arviat and Whale Cove between 1974 and 1979. A March 2024 review by retired Quebec justice André Denis, commissioned by the Oblates, concluded on the preponderance of evidence that he assaulted six children. Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami called his death without trial in April 2024 'a systemic failure of nation states and religious institutions'.

title: Colombia — Constitutional Court orders Medellín archdiocese to release priests' files
who: Archdiocese of Medellín; Salesian Inspectorate of San Luis Beltrán, Medellín
cover_up: Both the archdiocese and the Salesian province refused journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos's 2019 request for the records of 43 priests, calling them private; the archdiocese appealed the first-instance ruling against it.
what: In May 2019 journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos, author of 'Dejad que los niños vengan a mí', asked the Archdiocese of Medellín and the Salesians for the records of 43 priests, including complaints against them. After both refused, he filed tutela actions. On 3 March 2020 the Constitutional Court ruled that the information was semi-private and that the right to information prevailed, ordering the archdiocese to hand it over. In 2022 the Court agreed to review a further petition covering 915 priests who served in Medellín.

title: Ecuador — Fr César Cordero Moscoso, Cuenca
who: Archdiocese of Cuenca; schools founded by Cordero; Catholic University of Cuenca
cover_up: First accusations date from 2010, but he remained honoured; the case drew attention only in 2018 when the Cuenca city council planned to decorate him.
what: Cordero Moscoso founded the Catholic University of Cuenca and led it from 1970 to 2013. In 2018 five men reported he had abused them as children at a school he founded. The Archdiocese of Cuenca accepted their testimonies as credible and apologised, and after a report sent to Pope Francis the Vatican dismissed him permanently from the clerical state in October 2018. His statue and decorations were removed. He died in 2023 aged 95 without a criminal conviction.

title: Ecuador — 103 complaints of sexual violence against clergy (Ecuavisa)
who: Catholic clergy in Ecuador
cover_up: Victims' families said the church hierarchy refused to share information or file complaints with prosecutors itself, contrary to a National Assembly commission report on sexual violence against children in education.
what: A months-long investigation by Ecuavisa's Visión 360 counted 103 complaints of sexual abuse involving Ecuadorian clergy, with cases in Guayas, Pichincha, Azuay and Los Ríos, including those of Fr César Cordero and Fr Luis Intriago. A survivors' association demanded that such crimes be made imprescriptible, as approved in a referendum.

title: Paraguay — Fr Carlos Urrutigoity and the removal of Bishop Livieres
who: Diocese of Ciudad del Este
cover_up: After accusations in the US (a 2002 complaint over students at St Gregory's Academy in the Diocese of Scranton), he moved with his group to Ciudad del Este, where Bishop Rogelio Livieres made him vicar general in 2014. Pope Francis removed Livieres in 2014; Urrutigoity left in June 2015. La Nación reported at least five Argentine priests accused of abuse or crimes against humanity had sheltered in
what: Argentine priest Carlos Urrutigoity was accused in 2002 in the US of sleeping with boarding-school students, giving them alcohol and sexually abusing a recently graduated seminarian. He then moved to the Diocese of Ciudad del Este, Paraguay, and became its second-in-command in 2014. His case reportedly cost Bishop Livieres his post when Pope Francis removed him in 2014. He was moved back to Mendoza, Argentina, in June 2015. He has not been convicted.

title: Costa Rica — Fr Mauricio Víquez, convicted after fleeing to Mexico
who: Archdiocese of San José; Episcopal Conference of Costa Rica
cover_up: A San José civil court ordered Archbishop José Rafael Quirós, the Episcopal Conference and the church's property entity to pay 65 million colones; the victims' lawyer said the church knew from 2002 and did nothing. Three other complaints were declared time-barred.
what: Víquez, a former church spokesman on family issues, fled Costa Rica in 2018 when accusations surfaced, going via Panama to San Nicolás de los Garza, Mexico, where he was caught; he was extradited in 2021. The church expelled him from the clergy in 2019. In March 2022 he was sentenced to 20 years (6 for sexual abuse, 14 for rape) for abusing an 11-year-old boy in his parish in 2002–2003. In August 2022 a civil court ordered the archbishop and two church entities to pay about US$100,000 in damages.

title: Puerto Rico — Arecibo priests defrocked; island-wide probe
who: Diocese of Arecibo; at least four Puerto Rican dioceses
cover_up: Prosecutor Yolanda Pitino said the diocese's information was insufficient and it had not answered requests for more; Justice Secretary César Miranda warned he might charge church officials suspected of withholding information.
what: In early 2014, after reports in El Nuevo Día, Bishop Daniel Fernández disclosed that since 2011 he had expelled six priests accused of sexual abuse in the Arecibo diocese. Local prosecutors said at least 11 other priests on the island were under investigation, and the Justice Secretary said at least four dioceses were being investigated. U.S. Homeland Security Investigations requested information.

title: Uruguay — Episcopal Conference apology
who: Episcopal Conference of Uruguay
cover_up: The abuses, about 20 years earlier, went unpunished because the statute of limitations had expired.
what: In April 2016 Uruguay's bishops apologised, expressing 'pain and shame', after receiving reports the previous year of three people abused by priests as teenagers. Auxiliary Bishop Milton Troccoli said one priest left the priesthood and another was removed after an investigation; criminal charges were time-barred.

title: Honduras — Fr Joseph Maurizio, orphanage trips
who: Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown, Pennsylvania (Somerset County parish); orphanage in El Progreso
what: A Pennsylvania priest was found guilty by a U.S. federal jury in September 2015 on three of four counts of sexually abusing minors during trips to an orphanage in El Progreso, Honduras, between 2004 and 2009. He was also convicted of possessing child abuse material and of illegally transferring money to a charity to fund the trips.

title: El Salvador — Guatemalan priest arrested in San Salvador
who: Archdiocese of San Salvador
what: On 13 April 2019 Salvadoran police arrested Guatemalan priest José Venancio Boror Uz, 62, outside his parish in San Salvador; prosecutors charged him with sexual assault of a six-year-old girl and he was held in pre-trial detention. Archbishop José Luis Escobar announced the charge at Mass and apologised to the victim's family.

title: Japan — Bishops' Conference survey: 16 cases
who: Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan (16 dioceses)
cover_up: Eight accused clerics were transferred; some punished clerics kept working or moved to another diocese; five remained priests. Only one denied case was examined by a third-party panel.
what: The Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan began a survey of all 16 dioceses in May 2019 and published it on 7 April 2020. It found 16 cases of sexual abuse of minors from the 1950s to the 2010s, called 'the tip of the iceberg'. Most victims took 10 to 30 years to report, some 50 to 70 years. Of the accused, seven were Japanese priests and eight religious or missionaries, seven of them foreign. Earlier internal surveys (2002, 2012) had found two and five cases.

title: Sri Lanka — temple chief monk jailed for abusing boy brought for ordination
who: Sri Sambuddha Walukarama Temple (Theravada Buddhist)
what: The Anuradhapura Special High Court for Child Crimes convicted the 65-year-old chief incumbent of a temple in Thalakolawawa on three charges of sexually abusing a 14-year-old boy brought to the temple for ordination in May 2022. He received three 10-year terms, ordered to run concurrently (10 years effective) and Rs 500,000 compensation. The Attorney General's Department prosecuted after a Thambuttegama Police investigation.

title: Sri Lanka — senior Anuradhapura monk arrested (2026)
who: Malwathu Chapter (Theravada Buddhist)
what: In 2026 police arrested a senior Buddhist monk, a former chief prelate (Atamasthanadhipathi) of Anuradhapura, over allegations of sexually abusing an underage girl. The Malwathu Chapter suspended him from religious duties pending the case; he denies the allegations. Rights groups cited delays and accountability problems in cases involving senior monks.

title: Nigeria — Anglican priest jailed in Ekiti for defiling a five-year-old
who: Anglican Church (Church of Nigeria)
what: On 5 August 2019 an Ado-Ekiti High Court sentenced Anglican priest Gabriel Asateru, 53, to five years in prison and a N50,000 fine under the Ekiti State Child Rights Law for defiling a five-year-old girl on or about 23 December 2016 while visiting her parents in Ifisin-Ekiti.

title: Nigeria — Winners Chapel pastor given life for raping a minor (Ekiti)
who: Living Faith Church (Winners Chapel), Omuo-Ekiti
what: The Ekiti State High Court in Ado-Ekiti sentenced Enoch Gbinyiam, a pastor of Winners Chapel in Omuo-Ekiti, to life imprisonment for raping the daughter of a church member who visited the vicarage to help with chores, after sedating her drink. The conviction was under the state's Gender Based Violence (Prohibition) Law, 2019.

title: IICSA — Child protection in religious organisations and settings (2021)
who: 38 religious organisations in England and Wales, including churches, mosques, synagogues, temples and out-of-school faith settings
cover_up: The Inquiry found victim-blaming, discouraging external reporting and putting reputation above victims; some organisations serving large congregations had no child protection policy at all.
what: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse published its report on 2 September 2021 after taking evidence from 38 religious organisations. It found child sexual abuse in most major UK religions and 'shocking failings' in prevention and response. An estimated 250,000 children attend faith-based supplementary or out-of-school settings, which need not register with any state body and have no child-protection oversight. Among cases heard, a mosque Qur'an teacher who abused four children aged about nine was convicted in 2017 and jailed for 13 years. It recommended that every religious organisation have a child protection policy and that the law on full-time education be changed so unregistered schools come under Ofsted.

title: Methodist Church (Britain) — Past Cases Review
who: Methodist Church in Britain
cover_up: The church said abuse by some Methodists had been ignored or not listened to; it issued an 'unreserved apology'.
what: Published on 28 May 2015 after three years of research, the Methodist Church's Past Cases Review found 1,885 cases of sexual, physical, emotional and domestic abuse or neglect going back to 1950. In 26% of cases church ministers or lay employees were identified as the alleged perpetrators. Six police investigations were ongoing. General Secretary Martyn Atkins made an unreserved apology.

title: Bob Jones University — GRACE report
who: Bob Jones University (independent fundamentalist Christian)
cover_up: Several victims said campus counselors did not report their abuse to legal authorities; counseling blamed victims and treated all 'sexual sin' as equal. The university fired and then rehired GRACE during the investigation.
what: Bob Jones University hired GRACE (Godly Response to Abuse in the Christian Environment) in November 2012 to review its handling of sexual abuse. GRACE's roughly 300-page report, released 11 December 2014, found the school responded to abuse claims with ignorance of state reporting law, little trauma training and a culture that blamed victims; some counselors encouraged victims to repent. The review was prompted in part by a board member's handling of a 1997 case in which a minor girl raped by a church deacon in New Hampshire was made to confess before the congregation. The university president apologised.

title: Royal Commission Case Study 36 — Church of England Boys' Society
who: Church of England Boys' Society (now Anglican Boys' Society / Boys' Ministry Australia); Anglican dioceses of Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Tasmania
cover_up: Allegations were not reported to police at all or not in time; a parish priest told one victim to 'let sleeping dogs lie'. The report found Peter Hollingworth, former Archbishop of Brisbane and later Governor-General, made 'a serious error of judgment' in letting an accused priest continue in ministry.
what: The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse reported in February 2017 that the CEBS youth group gave paedophiles easy access to boys from the 1970s to the 1990s, with abuse on camps, sailing and fishing trips and overnight stays at rectories. It found 'networks of sexual perpetrators at CEBS who had knowledge of each other's sexual offending against boys and in some instances facilitated' it; several associated men were later convicted. It found a focus on protecting the reputation of the church, dioceses, CEBS and clergy.

title: Royal Commission Case Study 42 — Anglican Diocese of Newcastle
who: Anglican Diocese of Newcastle (Bishops Alfred Holland 1978–92, Roger Herft 1993–2005)
cover_up: Found a 'do nothing' approach under Bishop Holland and a 'weak and ineffectual' response under Bishop Herft; complainants were treated as liars and sometimes threatened with legal action; abusive relationships were misrepresented as consensual; dioceses receiving moved clergy were not warned; diocesan lawyers acted for accused priests. Former dean Graeme Lawrence was defrocked.
what: The Royal Commission's report, released on 7 December 2017 after hearings in August and November 2016, found systemic issues let a group of perpetrators operate in the diocese for at least 30 years. Fr Peter Rushton died in 2007 never charged, though the diocese acknowledges he was a child sex offender. Fr James Brown pleaded guilty in 2011 to 27 child sexual abuse charges relating to 19 boys and was jailed for up to 20 years. Bishop Herft resigned as Archbishop of Perth in 2016. Later bishops Brian Farran and Greg Thompson acted against alleged perpetrators and faced backlash.

title: Nigeria — Kaduna 'Islamic school' raid frees 300+ boys and men
who: Imam Ahmad Bun Hambal Centre for Islamic Studies (purported Islamic school / rehabilitation centre)
what: On 26 September 2019 Kaduna police raided a building signed as an Islamic studies centre and freed more than 300 boys and men, many chained and with whip scars. Some had been brought from Burkina Faso, Mali and Ghana; families said they were denied access. Seven people claiming to be teachers were arrested. Local media reported captives were tortured, starved and sexually abused. The raid led to further rescues from similar 'torture houses' in northern Nigeria.

title: Thailand — 'Jet-set monk' Wirapol Sukphol convicted of abducting and raping a girl
who: Wat Pa Khantitham forest monastery (Theravada Buddhist)
cover_up: He fled to the United States after a 2013 video exposed his lifestyle and was extradited back in July 2017.
what: Former abbot Wirapol Sukphol was convicted by Bangkok's Criminal Court in October 2018 of abducting a 13-year-old girl from her parents and sexually abusing her in 2000 and 2001; DNA matched him to a child the girl bore. He received 16 years, added to a 114-year term for fraud and money laundering imposed in August 2018. The court cited his flight to the U.S. as aggravating.

title: Thailand — Buriram abbot confessed to raping a girl from age 13
who: Wat Muang Doo (Theravada Buddhist); Buriram Provincial Office of Buddhism
cover_up: After confessing and being charged, the abbot paid the poor family 150,000 baht to withdraw the case and then reportedly fled to another province rather than be defrocked.
what: The 52-year-old abbot, who led school meditation sessions, took a 13-year-old girl from her school's nurse's office to his temple in 2015, drugged and raped her, and kept abusing her for five years under threat of releasing recordings. The abuse came to light in August 2019 when she was five months pregnant. He confessed and was charged with rape. The Provincial Office of Buddhism said he must be defrocked.

title: Thailand — Chiang Dao monks arrested for procuring a boy for an abbot
who: Temple in Chiang Dao (Theravada Buddhist)
what: On 19 June 2013 Chiang Mai police arrested two young monks, aged 20 and 23, accused of repeatedly taking a 14-year-old boy to a temple abbot for sexual services since February. Police said the two faced up to 15 years in jail; the abbot had not yet been arrested pending a warrant.

title: Kenya — Mombasa priest's conviction; sentence turned into sermons
who: Archdiocese of Mombasa
cover_up: On appeal the High Court set aside a seven-year sentence and replaced it with probation plus monthly sermons on the Sexual Offences Act; a Mombasa women's faith leader called it too lenient to deter predators.
what: Fr Dominic Muli Nzioka was convicted by a Mombasa magistrate in June 2023 of indecent assault on a 16-year-old girl whom he invited to his parish house in September 2020 and gave alcohol. On 7 March 2024 High Court Justice Anne Ong'injo upheld the conviction but set aside the seven-year sentence, ordering three years' probation during which he must preach on the Sexual Offences Act at least once a month.

title: Kenya — Kitale priest charged with defiling a 14-year-old
who: Catholic Diocese of Kitale
what: Fr Daniel Gitau Waweru was arraigned in Kitale in December 2024, accused of defiling a 14-year-old congregant between 2021 and 2022 while priest in charge of Kipsaina Catholic Church. He denied the charges. Police said the Kitale bishop convened a meeting that helped investigators complete evidence, and that the priest had been sent on leave during the inquiry.

title: Tanzania — Fr Sixtus Kimaro jailed 30 years
who: Catholic Church in Tanzania
what: In August 2006 Fr Sixtus Kimaro, 38, was jailed for 30 years for sex offences against a 17-year-old boy over two years; the BBC called it the first such case reported in Tanzania. The magistrate rejected a plea for leniency on account of his youth.

title: South Africa / Germany — Fr Georg Kerkhoff, youth camp abuse and extradition
who: German-language Catholic community, Randburg; dioceses in Germany (Lower Rhine)
cover_up: He went to South Africa with cases pending in Germany and worked there for years; the Southern African bishops said they had not invited or appointed him. After his 2013 arrest he was bailed into the care of the Eshowe diocese.
what: A German priest wanted in Germany on an international warrant was arrested in September 2013 outside a court in Brits, South Africa, where he was on trial for indecent acts in 2008 against four boys aged nine and ten at a German-language Catholic youth camp near Johannesburg. After extradition, the Krefeld district court in early 2015 sentenced him to six years on 25 counts of sexually abusing boys in his Lower Rhine parishes, including his godson from 2001. South African families prepared compensation claims.

title: South Africa — Jericho Apostolic Church priest given life
who: Jericho Apostolic Church, Mhluzi
what: A Sexual Offences Court sentenced Sipho Matthew Manana, 47, a priest at Jericho Apostolic Church in Mhluzi, to life imprisonment for raping a 12-year-old boy twice in August 2011. The magistrate found he groomed the boy, from a poor single-parent home, with gifts and money.

title: DR Congo — Tshumbe diocese priest accused; court exonerated
who: Diocese of Tshumbe
what: A girl told reporters in January 2023 that a priest of the Tshumbe diocese raped her about two years earlier, when she was 14 and aspiring to religious life. A church source said the Holy See sent investigators, the priest was suspended and the case went to Congolese courts, which 'exonerated' him; the Vatican probe found no evidence. Her lawyer said she had fled to Gabon and intended to appeal. Ending Clergy Abuse asked Pope Francis to act during his visit.

title: Philippines — Baguio diocese finance officer convicted of raping a scholar
who: Diocese of Baguio
cover_up: He fled after the arrest warrant was issued and was a fugitive for about a year before surrendering on 25 June 2024.
what: Fr Mark Elis Batolne, the diocese's finance officer and head of its radio station, was convicted in December 2025 by Baguio's Regional Trial Court Branch 2 (Family Court) of three counts of raping a 16-year-old church scholar who did chores at the Bishop's Residence, in March 2023. He received 20 to 40 years per count and was ordered to pay damages. The girl reported to her school principal in May 2023.

title: Brazil — three Arapiraca priests convicted (Penedo diocese)
who: Diocese of Penedo
cover_up: According to the victims, Bishop Valério Breda knew what was happening; he suspended the priests two days after the scandal broke. The convicted priests were not jailed pending appeal.
what: On 19 December 2011 a juvenile court judge in Arapiraca convicted Monsignor Luiz Marques Barbosa (21 years), Monsignor Raimundo Gomes and Fr Edílson Duarte (16 years 4 months each) of abusing altar boys. The case began with complaints from former altar boys in March 2010 and a secretly filmed video broadcast on SBT television.

title: Brazil — Santa Luzia priest sentenced to 43 years
who: Paróquia São Benedito; a religious school in Santa Luzia
what: On 15 October 2024 a court sentenced Fr José Carlos Pereira to 43 years and 6 months for sexual crimes against four people, including a girl he first abused at age 13 in 2014 in the parish office. The parish removed him in 2021 when the complaints surfaced. The judge said his religious influence over families delayed complaints. He was allowed to appeal in liberty.

title: Mexico — bishops say 152 priests removed in nine years
who: Mexican Episcopal Conference (CEM)
cover_up: The CEM president said there was no national count of victims because 'each bishop handles these problems' and no central record exists.
what: On 10 February 2019 Archbishop Rogelio Cabrera of Monterrey, president of the Mexican Episcopal Conference, said 152 priests had been removed from ministry in the previous nine years after being found guilty of sexually abusing minors, some of whom were jailed. He said there was no exact figure for victims.

title: Mexico — Fr Luis Esteban Zavala sentenced to 65 years
who: Catholic Church in Mexico
what: Catholic priest Luis Esteban Zavala Rodríguez was sentenced to 65 years and three months in prison for aggravated rape and corruption of minors (reported February 2021).

title: Amish bishop charged for not reporting abuse confession (Lancaster County)
who: Old Order Amish church district, Lancaster County
network: Amish and Old Order Anabaptist church districts
cover_up: Witnesses said the bishop had the matter 'handled internally' to keep it quiet; the church excommunicated the abuser but did not notify police.
what: In April 2020 Amish bishop Levi Esh Sr., 63, was arraigned on felony and misdemeanour charges for failing to report a church member's confession to sexually assaulting three girls around 2012–2013. Pennsylvania law requires clergy to report child abuse.

title: Amish bishop pleads guilty to failure to report (Dauphin County)
who: Amish church district, Dauphin County
network: Amish and Old Order Anabaptist church districts
cover_up: Told of two abuse cases in 2011, the bishop did not report them and told police he had been told one 'wasn't really that bad'.
what: Amish bishop Christ M. Stoltzfus, 70, pleaded guilty in Dauphin County court in September 2017 to failure to report child abuse and received three months' probation. A church member had told him in 2011 about two cases of child sexual abuse by another member; state police began investigating in January 2017 after a confidential tip.

title: Greece — retired Orthodox priest jailed for abusing an 11-year-old
who: Church of Greece (retired priest)
what: In September 2021 the Larissa Mixed Jury Court of Appeals sentenced an 83-year-old retired priest to eight years for sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl, and her 30-year-old mother to five years for complicity, after she handed over the girl in exchange for money and goods. He was allowed to serve the term under house confinement on health grounds.

title: Russia — Hieromonk Meletiy (Tkachenko) jailed 17 years, Sakha
who: Russian Orthodox Church, Sakha Eparchy
what: A Sakha district court on 28 November 2018 sentenced Hieromonk Meletiy (Andrei Tkachenko) to 17 years in a maximum-security prison for sexual violence against children. He was detained in June 2017 over two minors; investigators later said he abused 87 children under 14. The eparchy suspended him and said it would seek his removal after appeals.

title: Russia — Fr Gleb Grozovsky, Orthodox youth camps; fled to Israel
who: Russian Orthodox Church (Orthodox youth camps)
what: A court in the St Petersburg area sentenced former priest Gleb Grozovsky on 17 January 2018 to 14 years for violent sexual acts against minors at Orthodox youth camps in 2009 and 2013, and ordered 400,000 roubles compensation to each of three victims' families. After police opened a case in November 2013 he fled to Israel, was detained there and extradited; he had been in custody since September 2014.

title: Myanmar — Pathein monastery: four schoolgirls raped
who: Saitta Thuka monastery (Theravada Buddhist monastic boarding)
cover_up: The monk disappeared when parents went to police; TIME found police unable or unwilling to say whether a search continued, and described near-blanket immunity for monks, with police deferring to the religious affairs ministry and the Sangha. An ex-monk who reprimanded him was told to move away.
what: Four girls aged 10 to 14 staying free at a monastery so they could attend school were repeatedly raped from June 2017 by the monastery's administrator monk, according to the children and families interviewed by Myanmar Now. The abuse came to light in February 2018; police issued orders to arrest him on sight across several regions. TIME reported up to 300,000 children may live in Myanmar monasteries, with few records kept.

title: Romania — former Bishop of Huși jailed for raping a seminary pupil
who: Romanian Orthodox Church, Diocese of Huși; Huși Orthodox Theological Seminary
cover_up: The case surfaced in June 2017 when the bishop himself complained to anti-corruption prosecutors that three priests were blackmailing him with a recording; a former archimandrite was earlier jailed for that blackmail.
what: Romania's High Court of Cassation and Justice upheld a Galați Court of Appeal ruling sentencing former Bishop Corneliu Bârlădeanu (Cornel Onilă) to eight years for rape and other sexual assaults, in a case that began with 2017 recordings allegedly showing him with a minor pupil of the Huși seminary. Former archimandrite Sebastian Jitaru received 14 years 2 months for rape and sexual assaults. The diocese and seminary were ordered to pay court costs; the diocese apologised to the victims. Bârlădeanu resigned in August 2017. Media described him as the first senior Romanian Orthodox hierarch to go to prison.

title: Nicaragua — Fr José Leonardo Urbina sentenced for raping a 14-year-old
who: Diocese of Granada (Nicaragua)
what: On 2 September 2022 a Managua court specialising in violence against women sentenced Fr José Leonardo Urbina Rodríguez, 51, parish priest in Boaco, to 30 years (the legal maximum; component sentences totalled 49) for two counts of sexual abuse in December 2021 and January 2022 and the rape of a girl under 14. He was arrested in July 2022 on her mother's complaint. The Granada diocese expressed 'deep pain' at the sentence. The case came amid the Ortega government's prosecutions of priests; an exiled lawyer criticised aspects of the trial.

title: India — Kerala priest given double life (Kottapuram diocese)
who: Diocese of Kottapuram
cover_up: The priest's brother was jailed for helping him hide after the police case was registered; a government doctor who examined the girl was found guilty of failing to report the abuse.
what: On 8 December 2016 a POCSO special court in Ernakulam gave Fr Edwin Figarez double life sentences and a fine of Rs 225,000 for repeatedly raping a 14-year-old girl from January to March 2016 under the pretext of music lessons. Police registered the case on 1 April 2016 after the girl told her mother; he went into hiding and later surrendered.
